question: GQ-006
subject: turning "36 failing jobs" from a count into a diagnosis
why: Last loop I reported 36 failing jobs and said plainly it was a count, not 36 defects, because I had traced exactly one. So I traced the two largest groups.

exit_127.mechanism: launchd starts /bin/bash successfully; bash then cannot find the script it was told to run. Verified directly: `bash /tmp/definitely-not-here.sh` returns exactly 127.
exit_127.note: The interpreter existing is why this is not exit 78. The failure is one layer deeper than launchd.

exit_78.mechanism: EX_CONFIG — launchd cannot start the program at all. No crash, no traceback, log stays 0 bytes.

combined.cause: The program or script the job points at has been deleted.
combined.reading: 25 of 26 failures in the two largest groups are the same defect: files removed without the launchd jobs that reference them being unloaded. This is not 26 independent problems.

still_untraced.note: Not examined. Reported as a residual rather than folded into the diagnosis.

one_exception: A single exit-78 job whose program does exist. Not diagnosed — it fails for a different reason and I have not found it.
not_fixed: Nothing repaired or unloaded. Deleting a launchd job is destructive and these are operational, not Library artifacts.
